In the "Kent 20", on May 8th, our team repeated their performance in the Finchley 20 by running S.L.H. a close second. Sid Ring was second to T.

Archie Bedford finished third in the individual race with Vern Blowfield in fifth place, and then came Jimmy Wood 13th with Len Bishop 16th, and the latter just beat Tom Richards, the well known marathon runner.

With excellent weather and with such fine runners as the Blackheath trio Reynolds, Piper and Busby and Tom Richards, Paterson and Henning competing, it was generally anticipated that Ballington's record would be in danger, and Reynolds put up a magnificent performance in lowering it by 1 min. 20 sec…
At the end of the first of the three laps, Dave Fotheringham, of T.V.H., was leading from Geoff Iden, of Victoria Park H., with Tom Richards, of S.L.H., in third place.

The first three men home were all inside the 3 hours 57 minutes 5 seconds target set by Tom Richards in 1956. And the new lap record holder, Ron Linstead (Belgrave Harriers) smashed the previous best by 6 minutes 25 seconds!....

Tom Richards's record was smashed by 6¼ minutes with a display of running which led the front page of the I.O.M. "Daily Times" to say "...but if he was unfamiliar with the circuit he was certainly unafraid of the T.T. course's reputation".
Cabrera (Argentine) and our old friend, Tom Richards of S.L.H. On crossing the line for the bronze medal E'tienne was whipped on to a stretcher.

On his return to Belgium he became one of the heroes of the 1948 Olympic Games. Étienne (Steve) Gailly was first into Wembley Stadium for the finish, but was so exhausted that Cabrera (Argentine) and Britain's own Tom Richards (S.L.H.) passed him on what must have seemed an endless lap of the track.

The grand finale, the Marathon, provided its usual high drama with Cabrera of Argentina catching Belgium's Etienne Gailly four hundred metres from the tape closely, followed by Britain's Tommy Richards, who had run a very sensible race.

Tommy Richards was looking stronger as the race progressed and with just 2 kms. remaining it was impossible to predict the winner as just 16 seconds covered the Argentinian, the Belgian and the Welshman.

Etienne was first into the stadium but was overtaken by the winner, Cabrera of Argentina and then by Tom Richards of Britain. During the war years Etienne raced for the Club in several matches against Tom who ran for SLH.
